criticalFinding_slateAddressability.claim_in_dispatch: 8 rail keys are independently slateable; 40 new/confirmed PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE pairs are the deliverable.
criticalFinding_slateAddressability.measured_at_source: grep -rn 'resolveAllowlist(' across artifacts/api-server/src (excluding tests): every call site passes a SINGLE LITERAL rail-key string, except cadRollServeCutover.ts's three helpers, which are typed to the 4 dollar rails / livingAreaSqft / yearBuilt only (unrelated). setbacksFactServeCutover.ts:52-56 -- the ONLY wrapper touching this dispatch's 4 Ft-suffixed rail names -- calls resolveAllowlist exactly ONCE per request, with the literal constant SETBACK_FRONT_FT_RAIL_KEY ('setbackFrontFt'). No call site anywhere passes 'setbackSideFt', 'setbackRearFt', or 'setbackCornerFt' to resolveAllowlist -- confirmed by a second grep restricted to those three literal strings, matching only parcelRecordAllowlist.ts's own doc comment, setbackRulesFactRead.ts (an unrelated companion-row constant list), and setbacksFactFromParcelRecord.ts itself.
criticalFinding_slateAddressability.whatThisMeans: This is NOT a gap -- it is PARCEL-B-SLATE3's own documented design (parcelRecordAllowlist.ts's module doc, 2026-09-04): 'Each three/four-key group is gated on ONE representative rail key... rather than seven independent slate entries.' setbacksFactFromParcelRecord.ts reads side/rear/corner directly off their own parcel_record cells (scalarNumberOrNull, no allowlist check) ONCE the group's single gate (setbackFrontFt's own (county) pair) resolves to 'record'. A PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE entry literally spelled '48021:setbackSideFt' would be inert prose -- no code anywhere would ever read it. Adding it would be the exact vacuous-compliance defect this program exists to close (S4's parcelAreaSqFt precedent, cited in this dispatch's own MISSION section), just relocated from a write path to a slate entry.
criticalFinding_slateAddressability.consequence_for_this_card: Of the 8 named rail keys, only 5 are independently slate-addressable: setbackFrontFt (representative for its 4-key group), setbackRules, maxHeightFt, maxLotCoveragePct, maxFootprintSqFt. setbackFrontFt is ALREADY IN PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE for all 5 in-scope counties (added 2026-09-04 by PARCEL-B-SLATE3, ahead of any passing verdict, exactly as that card's own doc comment anticipated) -- so it needs zero new Set entries; only its GATE needed to flip, and Z2 just flipped it. This card's only genuine, non-vacuous Set edit is the 4 remaining independent rails x 5 counties = 20 new entries. setbackSideFt/RearFt/CornerFt get zero entries, not because they are excluded from being served, but because they are ALREADY served -- see liveProbe_preEdit below, taken BEFORE any code change in this lane.
criticalFinding_slateAddressability.reconciliation: 40 named pairs = 40 real (county,rail) GATE pairs (Z2's own count, confirmed above) but only 25 of them are SLATE pairs at all (5 counties x setbackFrontFt, already present; 5 counties x 4 new independent rails, added by this card) because the slate's unit is 'group', not 'rail', for the 4-key setback family. 15 of the 40 named pairs (setbackSideFt/RearFt/CornerFt x 5 counties) have no slate unit of their own by design and are correctly outside this card's Set edit. Flagging this discrepancy per DEV_PROCESS 3.2/1.4 rather than silently padding the Set to hit a round number, or silently doing less than the dispatch asked without saying so.
